summary: This program models a printer's waiting list using a Queue, adding four documents and then handing them off one at a time in the order they arrived. Before each job prints, it reports how many are still waiting and which one is next.

lines.text: Queue is the interface that describes first-in, first-out behaviour, which is exactly how a real print queue works.
Queue is only an interface, so you need a concrete class that implements it; LinkedList is the usual choice for a simple queue.
The variable is declared as a Queue even though the object is a LinkedList, which limits you to queue-style operations and keeps the intent of the code clear.
offer adds an element to the back of the queue; it is the queue's polite version of add and returns false instead of throwing an exception if the queue refuses the item.
A queue can still be looped over to inspect its contents, and this walks the jobs from front to back without removing any of them.
The total is captured before any processing starts, because size() shrinks with every job removed and would no longer be the original count.
The \n escape sequence inserts a blank line before the heading, separating the two sections of output.
The loop keeps going as long as jobs remain, and since each pass removes exactly one job, it is guaranteed to end.
peek looks at the element at the front of the queue without removing it, which is how you check what is next before committing to it.
poll removes and returns the front element, so the job is taken off the queue and saved so it can be reported as printed.
